drg.description: Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC

notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed. 47-year-old female admitted for urinary tract infection. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.89, creatinine 0.71, hemoglobin 13, platelets 245, sodium 140, wbc 5.7; vitals dbp 66-69, heart_rate 76-80, map 84-86, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 14-16, sbp 120-124, spo2 97-98, temp 36.9-37.1
Day 0 orders/meds/results: Urinalysis: positive nitrites, >50 WBC/hpf; Ceftriaxone 1 g IV; Normal saline 1 L IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 0.68, hemoglobin 12.2, platelets 245, sodium 140, wbc 5.9; vitals dbp 64-70, heart_rate 75-79, map 84-88, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 14-16, sbp 120-126, spo2 97-98, temp 36.8-37
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 47-year-old female, length of stay 3 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Urinary tract infection. Follow up with primary care in one week. Patient seen and examined at bedside.
